title: Colder surroundings go with less REM, because temperature control slips in that phase
summary: NHLBI says people usually have more REM later in the night, and less REM in colder temperatures, because the body does not regulate temperature properly during REM.
body: The stages page says REM is usually heavier later in the night. It also says a person does not have as much REM in colder temperatures. The reason it gives is that, during REM, the body does not regulate its temperature properly. That is a statement about the phase, not a room-temperature prescription for a nursery. Safe-sleep pages about overheating a baby are a different claim.

sources.title: How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages
